questions.q: Classify: 'What a beautiful painting this is!'
questions.a: Exclamatory — it exclaims admiration, it does not ask. A wrong answer 'interrogative' reveals the student reads 'what' as question-automatic — the exclamation mark and the admiring tone are the real signals.

questions.q: Convert to interrogative: 'She finished the puzzle.'
questions.a: 'Did she finish the puzzle?' A wrong answer 'She finished the puzzle?' relies on intonation alone — boards want the proper inverted form.

questions.q: Which is imperative: 'The window is open' / 'Is the window open?' / 'Open the window' / 'How open the window is!'
questions.a: 'Open the window' — it gives a command; the subject 'you' is understood. A wrong answer picking the exclamatory shows the student matches keywords, not jobs.

questions.q: Sentences do four jobs and each job has a name: declarative (states), ______ (asks), imperative (commands/requests), exclamatory (exclaims).
Fill in the blank: Sentences do four jobs and each job has a name: declarative (states), ______ (asks), imperative (commands/requests), exclamatory (exclaims).
Fill in the blank: Line up four ______ about one event: 'You scored a goal.' / 'Did you score a goal?' / 'Score a goal!' / 'What a goal!' Same event, four jobs.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student names the type of any sentence from its job and punctuation, converts one type into another, and punctuates each correctly (. ? !).
